chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no salat in the two Eids except with an Imam; and if you pray by yourself, then there is no harm.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: an Imam, the leader with whom the Eid prayer is held
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eids, meaning Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.بَأْسَ: harm or objection; here meaning there is no problem
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: salat, the ritual prayer being discussed here
key_terms.وَحْدَكَ: by yourself, individually and not in congregation

ai.seo_question: Is salat al-ʿĪdayn only valid with an Imam, and can it be performed individually?
ai.summary: This hadith states that salat of the two Eids is not established as an obligatory congregational prayer except with an Imam. It also indicates that if a person performs it alone, there is no harm in doing so.
